filled_prompt:
Task: Author Name Disambiguation (AND)
prompt_version: v1
output_schema_version: v1

Determine whether the ANCHOR and CANDIDATE refer to the same real-world person.

EVIDENCE CARD (JSON):
{
  "task": "AND",
  "anchor": {
    "author_norm": "example, author a.",
    "author_pos": 2,
    "record": {
      "eid": "2-s2.0-0000000001",
      "year": 2020,
      "source_title": "Example Journal of Studies",
      "title": "An example article title"
    },
    "coauthors_norm": ["coauthor, one", "coauthor, two"],
    "affiliations_norm": "example laboratory, example university, city, country",
    "authors_with_affiliations_norm": "coauthor, one, example laboratory, example university, city, country; example, author a., example laboratory, example university, city, country"
  },
  "candidate": {
    "author_norm": "example, author a.",
    "author_pos": 5,
    "record": {
      "eid": "2-s2.0-0000000002",
      "year": 2021,
      "source_title": "Another Example Journal",
      "title": "A different example article title"
    },
    "coauthors_norm": ["coauthor, three", "coauthor, four"],
    "affiliations_norm": "another department, another university, city, country",
    "authors_with_affiliations_norm": "coauthor, three, another department, another university, city, country; example, author a., another department, another university, city, country"
  }
}

DECISION RULES:
1. Use ONLY the fields provided in the evidence card above. No external knowledge.
2. Author(s) ID is NOT provided and must NOT be inferred or assumed.
3. Positive signals:
   - High name similarity (author_norm) combined with co-author overlap.
   - Same or closely related affiliation across nearby publication years.
   - Overlapping linked author names in authors_with_affiliations_norm.
4. Negative signals:
   - Different affiliations across many years with no co-author overlap.
   - Clearly different publication venues or research contexts (source_title).
   - Very different co-author sets with the same name but different institutions.
5. Use "uncertain" when:
   - Evidence is ambiguous, missing, or contradictory.
   - Name matches but all other fields are absent.
   - Co-author and affiliation signals conflict.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
Respond with ONLY a single JSON object — no markdown code blocks, no preamble, no trailing text.

{
  "label": "match" | "non-match" | "uncertain",
  "confidence": <float 0.0-1.0>,
  "evidence_used": [<list of field names>],
  "reason_code": <snake_case string>,
  "abstention_reason": <string or null>
}
